title: ZIA Terraform operations that take several API writes with no rollback

checks.do: Whether the live object matches the configuration after a failed apply: read it (the list, the cluster and its nodes, the category's entries, the user's enrollment) before retrying.
Whether another writer's change to a list survives the delta write, since the delta is computed from an earlier read.
Whether a static IP for the address exists after a failed static IP create: list the static IPs for the address.
Whether the cluster's node list is still attached after a failed cluster delete: check the cluster's node list.

delta-helpers-read-then-add-then-remove.statement: The SDK's malicious-URL and exempted-URL updaters do not send the desired list. Each reads the current list, computes additions and removals locally, then sends the additions as one write and the removals as a second write, in that order. An error from either write is returned immediately.

delta-partial-apply.statement: When the addition write succeeds and the removal write fails, Terraform reports an error but the list already holds the additions and still holds the entries meant to be removed. Nothing in the helper undoes the first write. For the authentication settings list this is an exempted-URL list.
delta-partial-apply.conditions: The sequence is in the quoted code. That the first write stays committed depends on the API applying each ADD_TO_LIST or REMOVE_FROM_LIST call as it arrives and not holding it until activation; the absence of any compensating call is read from the two helper functions, not searched across the SDK.

delta-stale-snapshot.statement: The additions and removals are computed from a list read earlier in the same call, so a change another writer makes between the read and the writes is not seen by the delta.
delta-stale-snapshot.conditions: Follows from the read preceding the writes. Whether another writer's entries are then lost depends on how the API applies ADD_TO_LIST and REMOVE_FROM_LIST (gap concurrent-edit-overwrite). A removal of an entry only the other writer added is the case the delta cannot see; an addition the other writer also made is likely harmless.

custom-category-partial-state.statement: If the removal succeeds and the addition fails, the category has lost its old entries and does not hold the new ones, and the apply reports an error. Because a category's entries decide which category a URL falls into, the half-applied category changes rule matching for those URLs until a later apply repairs it.

partial-apply-leaves-neither-old-nor-new.statement: When the second write of a delta update or of a custom category update fails, the object on the server holds neither its previous contents nor the intended ones: the additions are present while the entries meant to be removed remain, or the old entries are gone while the new ones are absent.
partial-apply-leaves-neither-old-nor-new.conditions: Describes the server-side object after the second write fails. A following plan starts from that state only if it refreshes the resource from the API before comparing with configuration; the refresh behavior of these resources was not read.

delta-lists-are-commonest-sequence.statement: Among the multi-request sequences found in the searched ZIA code, the list-by-delta shape is the most frequent: four sequences send ADD_TO_LIST and REMOVE_FROM_LIST writes (malicious URLs, exempted URLs, custom URL categories, predefined URL categories), two send paired writes to different endpoints (security policy lists, browser control), and Virtual Service Edge cluster deletion, static IP coordinate discovery and user enrollment are one sequence each.
delta-lists-are-commonest-sequence.conditions: A count over the sequences listed in multi-write-places and the claims above; it is exactly as complete as that search, and sequences are counted by the shape of their write pattern, not by number of resources or call sites.

concurrent-edit-overwrite.title: Whether a write built from an earlier read overwrites another writer's change
concurrent-edit-overwrite.blocks: saying whether the delta and detach helpers can lose a concurrent edit
concurrent-edit-overwrite.detail: With two API clients: read a list or rule, change it from the second client, then let the helper write. Check whether the second client's change survives for an ADD_TO_LIST or REMOVE_FROM_LIST call and for a full-rule PUT.
